title: Weekly Project Meeting - Agape / HotWax
summary:
The meeting focused on safely upgrading the production environment, validating the new version in parallel, and managing the transition of project knowledge and responsibilities.

Mohammad Kathawala is preparing deployment documentation and scripts covering server setup, application deployment, database migrations, MQTT configuration checks, and startup without disrupting staging. Local environments for both application versions are documented and functioning, including Orders, BlackBrick screens, and local MQTT testing. The team agreed to synchronize Patrick Frea’s old-version changes into the new-version branch until migration rather than merge new-version changes backward.

Production cutover requires coordination of DNS, kiosk destinations, tenant-specific broker data, HTTP and MQTT machine access, and database synchronization. The proposed approach is to operate the upgrade server at `upgrade.agabeautomation.xyz`, mirror production REST requests into it, validate orders and subsequent changes in parallel, and later repoint production DNS. Patrick is designing the REST mirroring capability; kiosk screens may also be pointed to upgrade for observation.

The BlackBrick import-orders function currently requires approximately two to three minutes per order, compared with milliseconds for direct REST submission. Patrick indicated the importer may be outdated because the current JSON structure includes a barcode, and staging order JSON was provided to support local script updates.

DNS access remains constrained because Patrick is restoring access to his Whois.com account, while tenant delegation depends on DNS. The server is reachable by IP address, but using the IP temporarily as a domain remains under investigation. Database migration is expected to take hours, while DNS changes may require three or four days or longer.

Mohammad’s availability beyond the following week was uncertain, creating a significant transition risk. Patrick Frea said the project had entered its most sensitive phase and that he depended on Mohammad, Sunil, and Divesh for completion and handoff. The group concluded that additional labor would not eliminate the physical migration and coordination constraints, and Patrick preferred retaining Mohammad for approximately two additional weeks. Patrick Gibbons agreed to review extension and budget options, but the arrangement remained unresolved.
